//: Type gate for THIS package's own generated .d.ts files. Chained into the
`typecheck` script, so `npm run typecheck` (root and ts/) and the
ts-typecheck workflow all enforce it.
WHY A SECOND CONFIG. tsconfig.json sets skipLibCheck: true, and that is not
a preference — a dependency ships a .d.ts this package cannot compile:
node_modules/vite/types/importGlob.d.ts references the DOM `Worker` type
while `lib` here is ["ES2020"] with no DOM. Flipping the flag off on the
main config would red-x CI on code the repo does not control.
But skipLibCheck is all-or-nothing: it skips EVERY .d.ts, including the 544
in src/generated/ that this repo generates and publishes. So the main
typecheck was structurally incapable of seeing a broken generated binding,
and broken ones shipped to npm — PolicyEvaluation.overallStatus was typed
`PolicyStatus1` and IrPageSpec.apiAssertions `IrApiCheck[]`, names nothing
declared. Both compiled clean here.
WHAT THAT COST, PRECISELY. They reached the npm tarball but not dist/:
package.json has files: ["dist","src"], and none of the five affected
types (IrPageSpec, SpecCheckResult, PolicyEvaluation, TaskCompletionResult,
SpecApiEvent) is re-exported by any of the 18 tsup entry points. They
shipped as unreferenced src/generated/*.d.ts, reachable only by a deep-path
import, and no consumer writes one. So the defect was LATENT — it broke
nobody. The gate is still justified: which generated types get re-exported
is an ordinary editorial choice in src/*/index.ts that moves with every
schema addition, and the next broken binding that IS re-exported carries
the identical defect straight into dist/ and into every normal import.
This config is the narrow gate that closes the hole: same options,
restricted to the generated tree, with skipLibCheck OFF.
THE TWO DETAILS THAT MAKE IT WORK.
1. `include` names the .d.ts files explicitly. An ambient declaration file
is only type-checked when it is a program ROOT — merely being reachable
from a root is not enough, and a .d.ts reached that way is silently skipped
even with skipLibCheck: false. A gate that cannot go red is worse than no
gate, so the .d.ts glob is stated rather than implied.
2. `types: []` stops TypeScript auto-including every @types/* package, and
the narrow `include` keeps the test files (and therefore vitest -> vite)
out of the program. Together they are what keeps vite's uncompilable
importGlob.d.ts from failing a gate that is not about it.
(This key is ignored by tsc. It is a string array rather than a // comment
because .pre-commit-config.yaml runs check-json over *.json.)
